VibePascal v58 -- arm-linux NATIVE compiler (32-bit ARM, ARMHF/EABIHF; a 32-bit
Raspberry Pi OS is the target this exists for).  A .ppu shorter than its own
header says is truncated, and a half-written one can no longer hang the compiler.
Source commit: dedf242c696a543f9626e2839ced40876478a98a
Parent release for THIS target: v56 (a187bbac34)
Built: 2026-09-11, cross-built on x86_64-linux via a freshly bootstrapped
       compiler/ppcrossarm (md5 5e3d9ba2d978db06b31a1a15c37244d9, itself built
       from a CLEAN unit tree by the v58 native ppcx64,
       md5 8c8179b2f0a452cebec0131aa301b076), -dFPC_ARMHF at BOTH stages,
       BINUTILSPREFIX=arm-linux-gnueabihf-
Binary: bin/ppcarm  md5 49acd17c61202c72906a2a020091cac4
                    sha256 223468ae5fc8a3e8719dc6a9d56475bf7b6fca8693c5f6f6177305c679bd2db3
                    5670200 bytes, ELF 32-bit ARM EABI5, statically linked, stripped

ABI: ARMHF (EABIHF), hard float.  readelf reports flags 0x5000400, "Version5
EABI, hard-float ABI".  The compiler tree defaults to FPC_ARMEL, so this build
passes -dFPC_ARMHF explicitly; unchanged from v56.  It is NOT compatible with an
armel (soft-float) system.

BIN-ONLY, AND THE UNITS ARE NOT OPTIONAL.  This tarball contains the compiler and
nothing else.  Pair it with vibepascal-v54-arm-linux-units.tar.gz, which sits
beside it in this directory, stays valid, and is still REQUIRED -- this is a
refresh of an install, not a standalone one.

THIS TARGET SKIPPED v57.  x86_64 shipped v57 and v58 on 2026-09-11 while ARM
stayed at v56, so this release carries BOTH .ppu reader fixes, not one:

  v57 (c31227c8ca)  a half-written .ppu is an ERROR, not an infinite 99%-CPU spin
                    with no message.  On the v56 binary this replaces, a killed
                    build or a full disk could hang a compile forever.
  v58 (dedf242c69)  a .ppu SHORTER than the length its own header declares is
                    rejected instead of silently accepted.  v57 only noticed
                    damage it happened to trip over; lose the TAIL of a unit and
                    there was nothing to trip over, so the compiler built your
                    program against a unit that is not all there -- exit 0, no
                    message, nothing to search a log for.

THIS DOES NOT TURN GOOD BUILDS RED.  The rejection is soft and self-healing: a
truncated unit whose source is available is RECOMPILED and the build goes green;
a good copy in a later -Fu directory is used instead; only a truncated unit with
no source and no other copy stops the compile, and it stops with the message an
absent unit already gives.  Nobody is ever told to go and delete a file.

COMPILER BINARY ONLY.  No RTL change, no package change, no PPU FORMAT change
between v56 and v58 -- the reader got stricter, the format did not move.  The
v54 unit set stays valid.

VERIFIED ON THESE EXACT BYTES
-----------------------------
  * dist/ppu-truncation-check.sh ppcarm arm-linux, against the real 54211-byte
    packages/aspell/units/arm-linux/aspelldyn.ppu:
        12/25 offsets clean, 13 problem(s), exit 1   on the v56 binary this replaces
        25/25 offsets clean,  0 problem(s), exit 0   on this one
    Of the 13: 8 truncations HUNG and had to be killed at 30s, and 5 were
    ACCEPTED with rc=0 -- a corrupt unit taken as valid, silently.  The arm
    CROSS compiler scored 14 on the same file (9 HANG, 5 ACCEPTED): one offset
    that spins on the host binary errors out on the native one.  Reported as
    measured rather than rounded to match -- the ACCEPTED five, which are the
    silent half and the reason v58 exists, are identical on both.
    The pre-fix binary is the one that actually shipped as v56
    (md5 d9fd3cb9503e86206e2fdf456b62c61a), preserved and re-run this cycle
    under emulation -- not a reconstruction, and not an argument from source.
  * EXECUTION, not inspection.  This binary RUNS: qemu-arm-static reports
    version 3.3.1, target cpu arm, and it compiled and ran
        tests/test/tinlinevarnativeint1.pp -Munleashed -> VERDICT:PASS
        tests/test/tinlinevarstrinfer1.pp  -Munleashed -> VERDICT:PASS
        tests/test/tblockscopefinal1.pp                -> MATRIX: PASS
                                     (all corners block-scoped, released exactly once)
    and it correctly REJECTED both { %FAIL } tests, tinlinevar2 and tinlinevar3 --
    accepting those is the actual bug, so both directions are asserted.
  * dist/arm-runtime-proof.sh exercises this tarball end to end and checks the
    md5 above against the bytes it unpacks, so the number in this file cannot
    drift from the artifact without the proof failing.

NOT PROVEN HERE, AND SAID PLAINLY: qemu-user is an emulator.  It runs the real
shipped bytes and real ARM instruction encodings, so codegen and RTL defects DO
surface -- but it is not a Raspberry Pi.  NOBODY HAS RUN ANY VIBEPASCAL RELEASE
ON PHYSICAL ARM SILICON.  Do not quote a pass here as a hardware sign-off.
